display.purpose: Welcome wordmark only; 3.75rem on phone, 6rem from 640px.

headline.purpose: One onboarding question or results heading per screen; 2.25rem rising to 3rem.

title.purpose: Question prompts, section headings, planet names, verdicts; 1.5rem rising to 1.875rem.

numeral.purpose: Stats, ranks, XP, seconds, percentages; tabular figures, 1.875rem rising to 2.25rem.

body.purpose: Answers, explanations and promises; answers rise to 1.125rem from 640px.

label.purpose: Metadata, hints and stat labels in Moon Grey, sentence case.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: Secondary buttons and the answer feedback panel.

shadows.name: press
shadows.purpose: Primary button only; warm inset top edge.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions, route fill and reward rises.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Hover, press and answer-state transitions (built as 150ms utilities).

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Planet status changes and step transitions.

motion.name: flight
motion.purpose: Rocket flight between planets on the Galaxy map; the 1100ms --duration-flight token is not what the build uses.

motion.name: halo-spin
motion.purpose: Current planet's dashed halo; motion-safe only.

motion.name: timer-drain
motion.purpose: Orbit timer ring per second; disabled under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All animations and transitions collapse to 1ms; the rocket lands instantly.

narrative.overview:
A run is a voyage, not a quiz form. Every screen sits on the same deep-space ground: a near-black navy field with a quiet, static starfield and a faint indigo nebula at the top. Against it, twelve flat-vector planets carry all of the saturated colour, each with its own hue, and a single nova-yellow action per screen tells the player what to do next. Progress is always distance travelled along one dashed route, drawn the same way on the full Galaxy map and as the compact strip above every question.

Density is low and the type is large. Controls are rounded but firm, with soft offset shadows that lift them off the void instead of making them glow. Motion belongs to the voyage: the rocket flies the route, a flag plants on a finished planet, and the next planet wakes. Everything else stays still. The starfield never moves. Reduced motion is honoured: the rocket appears at its destination and state changes still read.

The build refuses the default trivia layout of a progress bar, a card and four pills on a grey field. Feedback is never carried by colour alone.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black navy ground, indigo surfaces, colour reserved for planets and four signal roles.
One nova-yellow primary action per screen.
Progress is a route through 12 named planets, dashed ahead and solid sky where travelled.
Bricolage Grotesque for headings, numbers and buttons; Figtree for reading.
Rounded-but-firm controls, soft offset shadows, a static starfield.
Large touch targets (44 to 64px) and icon plus label plus colour for every verdict.

rules.name: The One Nova Rule
rules.body: Each screen has exactly one Nova Yellow action. Everything else is secondary, ghost, or a planet.

rules.name: The Planets Own the Colour Rule
rules.body: Saturated hue belongs to the planets and the four signal roles. Surfaces, borders and text stay in the navy-indigo family.

rules.name: The Signal Meaning Rule
rules.body: Sky is position and time, Mint is correct, Coral is wrong or out of time. Never swap them for decoration.

rules.name: The Numbers Speak Bricolage Rule
rules.body: XP, scores, ranks, seconds and percentages are set in the display face with tabular figures, so they line up and feel like instruments.

rules.name: The Route Recurs Rule
rules.body: The voyage route is the progress indicator everywhere. The Galaxy map draws it as a curve through the planets; the mission bar and the Question screen repeat it as a 12-dot strip with a rocket over the current planet. Never substitute a percentage bar for voyage progress.

rules.name: The Ring Slot Rule
rules.body: A ringed planet's tilted ring overhangs about 1.1x the planet's diameter on each side, so a ringed planet needs a slot about 2.2x its diameter (render it smaller in a fixed slot: 0.46 versus 0.62 of the orbit-timer, 16 versus 22px in a 40px skill-map slot). Labels beside a planet clear whichever is larger, the ring or the current-planet halo (radius 66 on a 100 viewbox, 1.32x the planet's radius).

rules.name: The Still Sky Rule
rules.body: The starfield and nebula never move. Motion is spent on the voyage.

dos: Do show voyage progress as the dashed route (4 on 8) with the travelled part solid Sky, on the map, the mission bar and the Question screen.
Do keep exactly one Nova Yellow action per screen.
Do pair every verdict with an icon and a text label as well as Mint or Coral.
Do draw the countdown as the Orbit Timer, Coral at 5 seconds or less, seconds on a chip.
Do give ringed planets a slot about 2.2x their diameter and keep labels clear of the ring and the current-planet halo.
Do keep touch targets at least 44px, and 48 to 64px for primary controls and answers.
Do set numbers in Bricolage Grotesque with tabular figures.
Do respect reduced motion: land the rocket instantly and keep state changes legible.
donts: Don't use a generic percentage bar for voyage progress.
Don't animate or parallax the starfield.
Don't signal correct, wrong or time-up with colour alone.
Don't put saturated colour on surfaces, borders or body text; it belongs to planets and signals.
Don't use hard-edged or black-on-grey shadows; depth is navy and soft.
Don't set translucent list panels over scenery; the leaderboard list stays opaque.
